# Repository instructions

## Build, test, and lint

Run commands from the repository root. Use Node.js 24 LTS with npm and stable
Rust with `rustfmt` and `clippy`. Both `package-lock.json` and `Cargo.lock` are
committed. Native development also needs the platform prerequisites in
README.md: MSVC/Windows SDK/WebView2 on Windows, or Xcode Command Line Tools on
macOS Apple Silicon.

```sh
npm ci
npm run tauri dev                          # Full desktop app; starts Vite
npm run dev                                # Frontend server only, port 1420
npm run check                              # Strict TypeScript check
npm test -- --run                          # Frontend tests, non-watch mode
npm run build                              # TypeScript check and Vite build
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
npm run tauri build -- --no-bundle -- --locked  # Compile the native app
npm run tauri build -- -- --locked          # Package for the host platform
```

Targeted tests:

```sh
# One frontend file, or one test selected by its name
npm test -- --run src/editor.test.ts
npm test -- --run src/main.test.ts -t "does not overwrite an unreadable draft on Escape"

# Core-only suite, one integration-test file, or one exact integration test
cargo test -p journal-core --locked
cargo test -p journal-core --locked --test logging
cargo test -p journal-core --locked --test logging bom_and_multiline_unicode_are_preserved -- --exact

# One native-adapter unit test
cargo test -p obsidian-daily-logger --locked commands::tests::save_reloads_configuration_and_cannot_append_twice -- --exact
```

Frontend tests use Vitest with jsdom, configured in `vite.config.ts`.
`src/test-setup.ts` supplies the layout/selection stubs CodeMirror needs.
`src/main.test.ts` mounts the real UI with a typed mock `JournalApi`; it covers
settings, autosave, keyboard handling, and link completion. Rust integration
tests use synthetic notes and temporary vaults; native tests reuse
`config::test_support::fake_vault` and `note_path`. Keep real user configuration
and journals outside the repository. Graphical/WebKit behavior needs a manual
check with a disposable vault; jsdom and native compilation do not establish it.

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs checks and compiles the full app on Windows
x64, Windows ARM64, and macOS ARM64. Windows ARM64 packaging requires an explicit
`--target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`; do not infer the compiled architecture from
the installer name. Tauri merges `tauri.windows.conf.json` or
`tauri.macos.conf.json` into the shared configuration.

## Architecture

- **Frontend (`src`)**: framework-free TypeScript. `main.ts` only mounts the UI;
  `ui.ts` owns the journal lifecycle and coordinates the CodeMirror editor,
  autosave, and settings dialog. `api.ts` is the typed Tauri IPC/window boundary.
  `mountJournal(root, api)` injects that boundary and returns a cleanup function.
  Settings are composed from field factories in `settings.ts`.
- **Native adapter (`src-tauri`)**: `lib.rs` initializes the app and registers
  commands and OS close/quit handling. `commands.rs` owns session state, invokes
  blocking work off the async runtime, and prevents duplicate submissions.
  `config.rs` handles persisted configuration, recoverable settings forms, and
  core-to-IPC conversion; `draft.rs` stores drafts independently of vault
  configuration. `error.rs` maps core errors to serializable `{ code, message }`.
- **Journal core (`crates/journal-core`)**: has no Tauri dependency. It owns note
  selection, entry rendering/placement, and atomic file writes. `obsidian.rs`
  resolves the selected plugin's daily-note layout; `moment.rs` implements the
  supported Moment.js date-format subset; `vault_index.rs` scans note names and
  computes Obsidian-style wikilink targets. Rust owns filesystem access and local
  timestamps; the webview accesses them only through the adapter.

## Cross-file conventions and contracts

- **IPC changes must be wired end-to-end.** Add commands to `commands.rs`,
  `lib.rs`'s `generate_handler!`, and the command manifest in `src-tauri/build.rs`.
  The manifest generates `src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated/*`; grant the
  corresponding `allow-*` permission in `capabilities/main.json`. Update
  `JournalApi`, its implementation, and typed test mocks. IPC result fields use
  snake_case; JavaScript invoke argument keys use camelCase for Rust snake_case
  parameters (for example, `vaultRoot` for `vault_root`).
- **Keep the webview narrowly privileged.** The main window has explicit
  command/window/event permissions and a strict CSP. The folder picker is
  invoked from Rust via `tauri-plugin-dialog`, not through webview dialog or
  filesystem permissions. Keep CodeMirror mounted inside the open shadow root
  in `editor.ts`: its styles use constructable stylesheets there; mounting in
  the document would inject style tags blocked by `style-src 'self'`. Editor
  colors inherit CSS variables from `styles.css`; do not loosen CSP to style it.
- **Configuration has two read paths.** `config::load` strictly rejects unknown
  fields and wrong types; `read_form` salvages valid values and reports problems
  so Settings can explicitly repair the file. Configuration lives at Tauri's
  `app_config_dir()/config.json`, with `draft.txt` beside it. There is no default
  vault or alternate config-file selector. Preserve defaults for older configs:
  a missing `note_source` loads but cannot log until explicitly chosen and saved.
  Plugin detection is a dialog suggestion, not an automatic persisted migration.
  For new settings, update Rust config/form types and defaults, TypeScript
  types, field factories, affected main-window controls, `config.example.json`,
  and README.md together.
- **Resolve note layouts rather than hard-coding paths.** Reload configuration
  on submission and preference changes; reread the selected Obsidian plugin's
  settings on every layout lookup. Periodic Notes supports both the `daily`
  layout and the active calendar set's `day` layout; core Daily notes supports
  both forms of its enabled-plugin list. Use `NoteLayout` and the date-format
  parser for vault-relative paths. Status/headings use `locate_daily_note`
  (today, else yesterday regardless of fallback), while writing uses
  `select_daily_note` (yesterday only with fallback enabled). Never create daily
  notes. Capture local time once per submission; yesterday is the previous
  calendar date, not a 24-hour subtraction.
- **Preserve the README's note-writing contract.** Only outer-trim submitted
  entries with `trim_entry` (including its Python-compatible whitespace rule);
  preserve internal whitespace, Unicode, and line breaks. Heading matching is
  exact and case-sensitive, allowing trailing spaces/tabs; the section ends at
  the next heading of any level. This is text/regex behavior, including headings
  inside code fences, not Markdown-parser behavior. Preserve UTF-8 BOM and
  existing bytes, and choose inserted LF/CRLF separators from the first LF.
  Block entries need the blank line before `---` to avoid setext headings.
  Reuse `atomic_write` for existing notes and `atomic_write_or_create` for
  config/drafts: sync a same-directory temporary file, preserve permissions,
  and replace without truncating the destination.
- **Draft recovery and successful logging are separate states.** Drafts retain
  exact text even with invalid vault configuration; an empty draft deletes the
  saved file. A failed startup draft read blocks editing/autosave until reload.
  `ui.ts` tracks `busy`, `draftLoaded`, and `savedPath`; the backend independently
  tracks `Session.saved`/`exiting`. Mark an entry saved immediately after the
  journal write, before clearing the draft/exiting. A later close failure must
  never allow resubmission. Await in-flight autosave before submission,
  preference/settings operations, or exit. `operate` uses a nonblocking session
  mutex and returns `busy` on contention; read-only note indexing intentionally
  bypasses that lock. Autosave debounces at 1 second, caps continuous typing at
  10 seconds, and flushes on blur. OS close/quit emits `close-requested` for the
  latest draft, with a 3-second fallback preserving the last stored draft.
- **Keyboard handling crosses the shadow boundary.** Completion handles
  Enter/Tab/Escape before the window handler; respect `defaultPrevented`.
  Enter saves, Shift+Enter inserts a newline, and Escape preserves the draft
  and exits unless Settings or completion is open. Ignore IME composition and
  repeated save/exit keys. Synthetic editor key events in tests must be
  composed, bubbling, and cancelable. Formatting uses decorations, not text
  rewriting; restoring a draft must not add it to undo history.
- **Note completion is optional and read-only.** Scan names, not note contents;
  skip dot entries and symlinked directories, cap the scan at 20,000 notes, and
  cap ranked suggestions at 100. Rust computes targets using
  `.obsidian/app.json`'s `newLinkFormat`; TypeScript ranks/display suggestions.
  Reload the index on startup, after settings saves, and on link queries when
  it is older than 30 seconds. Index problems are reported through `problem`
  and console warnings without blocking typing.
- **Error codes drive UX.** Keep `error.rs` mappings and `api.ts`'s
  `CONFIG_ERRORS` classification aligned: the main window shows `Config error!`
  for repairable configuration failures, while Settings exposes details.
  Other failures preserve the draft and show their message. Render
  vault/config-derived names, headings, and errors as text, not interpolated HTML.
- **App version changes span both toolchains.** Keep the app version aligned in
  `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and
  `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`; the core crate has its own version. Packaging
  workflow artifacts are unsigned/ad-hoc signed, and releases are published
  manually from tag-build artifacts.
